concerns.text: Task T009b mandates raising an 'error' or 'warning' if N < 10 to trigger narrative mode. This violates FR-006 and Constitution Principle VII, which require the system to 'automatically switch' and 'pivot' gracefully, not halt execution. Raising an error breaks the pipeline flow required for the fallback mechanism.

Task T022 implements Multilevel Meta-Analysis (MLM) as a 'robustness check'. Constitution Principle VI and FR-005 explicitly mandate 'random-effects model' and 'Bonferroni correction' only. MLM is an unapproved statistical method not present in the spec or plan, constituting scope creep and a violation of the statistical integrity constraint.

Task T000-verif calculates hashes only for data files (mock/real studies). Constitution Principle V requires 'Every artifact under this project carries a content hash', including code artifacts. Failing to hash scripts/configs means code changes won't invalidate the state file, violating the Versioning Discipline.

Task T014 sets a 'skipped' status for N < 10 but does not invoke the narrative synthesis tasks (T015b/T015c). FR-006 and Constitution Principle VII require the system to 'automatically switch' to narrative synthesis. Leaving the pivot logic disconnected from the quantitative gate violates the mandatory fallback protocol.

The plan defines a single 'meta_analysis.py' module for multiple comparisons (FR-005). Tasks T021, T023, and T023b fragment this into separate, potentially conflicting implementations (Correction, Standard Bonferroni, Holm-Bonferroni) without a clear 'single source of truth' for the final report, risking inconsistent statistical outputs.

Task T007d-2 implements NLP logic to extract qualitative descriptors for the narrative pool. FR-001 and US-1 specify narrative synthesis is for when *no* (r, n) pairs exist. This task conflates 'missing data' with 'qualitative extraction', potentially forcing studies with valid (r, n) into a qualitative path if they lack text descriptors, violating the evidence hierarchy.
